bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷四十九 雜傳第三十七: 翟光鄴 馮暉 皇甫暉 唐景思 王進 常思 孫方諫
title.en: Volume 49 Miscellaneous Biographies 29: Di Guangye, Feng Hui, Huang Fuhui, Tang Jingsi, Wang Jin, Chang Si, Sun Fangjian
title.raw: 卷四十九 雜傳第三十七: 翟光鄴 馮暉 皇甫暉 唐景思 王進 常思 孫方諫 Volume 49 Miscellaneous Biographies 29: Di Guangye, Feng Hui, Huang Fuhui, Tang Jingsi, Wang Jin, Chang Si, Sun Fangjian

sentences.zh: 翟光鄴

translations.literal: Zhai Guangye
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Guangye

sentences.zh: 翟光鄴，字化基，濮州鄄城人也。

translations.literal: Zhai Guangye, courtesy name Huaji, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Guangye, styled Huaji, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 其父景珂，倜儻有膽氣。

translations.literal: His father Jing Ke was bold and daring.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing Ke was a man of dash and nerve.

sentences.zh: 梁、晉相距於河上，景珂率聚邑人守永定驛，晉人攻之，逾年不能下，景珂卒戰死。

translations.literal: When Liang and Jin faced each other on the Yellow River, Jing Ke led the assembled townspeople to hold Yongding Post. Jin forces attacked for more than a year without taking it; Jing Ke died fighting in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Jin faced off on the river. Jing Ke rallied the townsmen to hold Yongding Post. Jin besieged it a year and could not break it; Jing Ke fell in the last fight.

sentences.zh: 光鄴時年十歲，為晉兵所掠，明宗愛其穎悟，常以自隨。

translations.literal: Guangye was then ten years old, carried off by Jin troops; Mingzong loved his quick wit and always kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye was ten when Jin soldiers carried him off. Mingzong prized his sharp mind and kept him close.

sentences.zh: 光鄴事唐，官至耀州團練使。

translations.literal: Guangye served Tang and rose to training commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang he rose to training commissioner of Yao.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，歷棣沂二州刺史、西京副留守。

translations.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he successively held the prefectures of Di and Yi and was deputy defender of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Gaozu he was prefect of Di and Yi in turn and deputy defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 出帝已破楊光遠，以光鄴為青州防禦使。

translations.literal: After the Deposed Emperor had defeated Yang Guangyuan, Guangye was made defender of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Deposed Emperor had broken Yang Guangyuan, Guangye was made defender of Qing.

sentences.zh: 光鄴招輯兵民，甚有恩意。

translations.literal: Guangye gathered soldiers and people with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye rallied troops and civilians with real grace.

sentences.zh: 契丹滅晉，遣光鄴知曹州。

translations.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, they sent Guangye to govern Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ended Jin, they set Guangye to govern Cao.

sentences.zh: 許王從益入汴，以為樞密使。

translations.literal: When Prince Xu Congyi entered Bian, Guangye was made Privy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xu Congyi entered Bian, he was made Privy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖入京師，改右領軍衛大將軍、左金吾大將軍，充街使。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu entered the capital, Guangye was changed to Grand General of the Right Stern Guard and Grand General of the Left Golden Crow, and served as street commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu entered the capital and made him Grand General of the Right Stern Guard and Left Golden Crow and street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周太祖入立，拜宣徽使、樞密副使，出知永興軍，卒於官。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne, Guangye was appointed Palace Commissioner and Vice Privy Commissioner, then sent out to govern Yongxing army and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Taizu took the throne and named him Palace Commissioner and Vice Privy Commissioner, then sent him to govern Yongxing; he died in post.

sentences.zh: 光鄴為人沈默多謀，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Guangye was a man of few words and many plans, famed for filial devotion to his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye spoke little and plotted much, and was known for honoring his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 雖貴，不營財產，常假官舍以居，蕭然僅蔽風雨。

translations.literal: Though ennobled, he did not amass property, often borrowing official quarters to live in, bare enough only to keep off wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Though high in rank he built no fortune, lodging in borrowed government rooms, spare enough only to shed wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 雍睦親族，粗衣糲食，與均有無，而光鄴處之晏然，日與賓客飲酒聚書為樂。

translations.literal: He was harmonious with his kin, wore coarse clothes and ate plain food, sharing what he had with them, while Guangye himself remained at ease, daily drinking with guests and gathering books for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He kept kin close in coarse dress and plain fare, sharing all he had while he stayed easy, drinking with guests and piling books for joy.

sentences.zh: 其所臨政，務以寬靜休息為意。

translations.literal: In every post he governed, his aim was leniency, quiet, and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he ruled, he aimed at leniency, quiet, and ease.

sentences.zh: 病亟，戒其左右，氣絕以屍歸洛，無久留以煩軍府。

translations.literal: When his illness grew urgent he warned his attendants: when breath failed, carry the corpse back to Luoyang—do not linger and trouble the army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he told his men: when breath fails, bear my body to Luoyang—do not linger and burden the command.

sentences.zh: 既卒，州人上書乞留葬立祠，不許。

translations.literal: After he died the people of the prefecture petitioned to bury him there and raise a shrine; the court refused.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the prefecture petitioned to bury him locally and raise a shrine; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 馮暉，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Feng Hui was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui came from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 為效節軍卒，以功遷隊長。

translations.literal: He was a soldier of the Loyalty army and, by merit, was promoted to squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Loyalty army as a soldier and rose to squad leader by merit.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，與梁相距於河上，暉以隊長亡入梁軍，王彥章以暉驍勇，隸之麾下。

translations.literal: When Tang’s Zhuangzong entered Wei and faced Liang on the river, Hui as squad leader fled into the Liang army; Wang Yanzhang, finding Hui fierce and brave, placed him under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong entered Wei and faced Liang on the river. Hui fled from his squad into Liang ranks. Wang Yanzhang took his dash and kept him close.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，莊宗赦暉不問。

translations.literal: When Liang fell, Zhuangzong pardoned Hui and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Liang fell; Zhuangzong pardoned Hui and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 從明宗討楊立、魏王繼岌平蜀，累遷夔、興二州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Mingzong against Yang Li and the Prince of Wei Jiji in pacifying Shu, and was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Qiong and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Mingzong against Yang Li and joined Jiji in pacifying Shu, rising to prefect of Qiong and Xing.

sentences.zh: 董璋反東川，暉從晉高祖討璋，軍至劍門，劍門兵守，不得入，暉從佗道出其左，擊蜀守兵殆盡。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhang rebelled in Dongchuan, Hui followed Jin Gaozu to attack Zhang. The army reached Jianmen; Jianmen’s garrison held and they could not enter. Hui took another road out to its left and struck the Shu defenders until nearly all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang rebelled in Dongchuan. Hui marched with Jin Gaozu to Jianmen, which held shut. He swung left by another road and cut down the Shu garrison almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 會晉高祖班師，拜暉澶州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu withdrew the army, Hui was made prefect of Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu withdrew and made Hui prefect of Chan.

sentences.zh: 天福中，範延光反魏州，遣暉襲滑州，不克，遂入於魏，為延光守。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era Fan Yanguang rebelled at Weizhou and sent Hui to strike Hua prefecture. He could not take it, then entered Wei and held it for Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianfu, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Wei and sent Hui against Hua. Hui failed, entered Wei, and held it for Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 已而出降，拜義成軍節度使，徙鎮靈武。

translations.literal: Before long he came out and surrendered, was made military commissioner of the Yicheng army, and was transferred to govern Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he surrendered, was made commissioner of Yicheng, and was shifted to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 靈武自唐明宗已後，市馬糴粟，招來部族，給賜軍士，歲用度支錢六千萬，自關以西，轉輸供給，民不堪役，而流亡甚眾。

translations.literal: Since Tang’s Mingzong, Lingwu had bought horses and grain, drawn in tribal groups, and paid out to the soldiers—sixty million strings from the treasury each year. West of the Pass the transport supply wore the people out, and exiles were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Since Mingzong, Lingwu had traded for horses and grain, drawn tribes in, and paid the troops—sixty million a year from the treasury. West of the Pass the convoys broke the people, and exiles swarmed.

sentences.zh: 青岡、土橋之間，氐、羌剽掠道路，商旅行必以兵。

translations.literal: Between Qinggang and Tuqiao, Di and Qiang plundered the roads, and merchants had to travel with armed escort.
translations.idiomatic: Between Qinggang and Tuqiao, Di and Qiang robbed the roads, and merchants marched only under arms.

sentences.zh: 暉始至，則推以恩信，部族懷惠，止息侵奪，然後廣屯田以省轉餉，治倉庫、亭館千餘區，多出俸錢，民不加賦，管內大治，晉高祖下詔書褒美。

translations.literal: When Hui first arrived he won them with kindness and trust; the tribes felt his grace and raids ceased. Then he expanded garrison farming to cut transport costs, built more than a thousand storehouses and lodges, spending mostly from his own salary so the people paid no new levies. Within his circuit there was great order, and Jin Gaozu issued an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Hui came and ruled by grace and trust; the tribes took his favor and raids stopped. He widened garrison farms to spare the convoys, raised a thousand storehouses and lodges from his own pay without new levies, and brought the circuit to order. Jin Gaozu praised him by edict.

sentences.zh: 党項拓拔彥超最為大族，諸族向背常以彥超為去就。

translations.literal: Among the Tangut, Tuoba Yanchao was the greatest clan; whether tribes turned or held back usually followed Yanchao.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Tangut, Tuoba Yanchao was the greatest house; tribes turned or held by his lead.

sentences.zh: 暉之至也，彥超來謁，遂留之，為起第於城中，賜予豐厚，務足其意。

translations.literal: When Hui arrived Yanchao came to call on him. Hui detained him, built him a mansion in the city, and gave lavish gifts to satisfy his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao came to call. Hui kept him, built him a house in the city, and heaped gifts until he was content.

sentences.zh: 彥超既留，而諸部族爭以羊馬為市易，期年有馬五千匹。

translations.literal: Once Yanchao was detained, the tribes vied to trade sheep and horses; within a year there were five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: With Yanchao held, tribes traded sheep and horses in rivalry; within a year Hui had five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 晉見暉馬多而得夷心，反以為患，徙鎮靜難，又徙保義。

translations.literal: Jin saw that Hui had many horses and had won the tribes’ hearts, and instead took it as a worry; he was transferred to govern Jingnan, then again to Baoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin saw his horses and tribal favor and took alarm; he was moved to Jingnan, then to Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 歲中，召為侍衛步軍都指揮使，領河陽節度使，暉於是始覺晉有患己意。

translations.literal: Within the year he was summoned as commander of the Palace Foot Guard and held the He-Yang military commission; Hui then first sensed that Jin meant him harm.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was recalled as Palace Foot Guard commander with He-Yang; Hui first felt Jin’s mistrust.

sentences.zh: 是時，出帝昏亂，馮玉、李彥韜等用事，暉曲意事之，因得復鎮靈武。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor was muddled; Feng Yu, Li Yantao, and others held power. Hui bent his will to serve them and thereby regained Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was lost; Feng Yu and Li Yantao held court. Hui courted them and won Lingwu back.

sentences.zh: 時王令溫鎮靈武，失夷落心，大為邊患。

translations.literal: Wang Lingwen then governed Lingwu, lost the tribes’ hearts, and became a great border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lingwen held Lingwu, lost the tribes, and bred great border trouble.

sentences.zh: 暉即請曰：「今朝廷多事，必不能以兵援臣，願得自募兵以為衛。

translations.literal: Hui at once petitioned, saying: "The court now has many troubles and surely cannot send troops to aid your subject. I beg leave to raise troops myself for guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hui petitioned at once: "The court is beset and cannot send you troops. Let me raise my own guard.

sentences.zh: 」乃募得兵千餘人，行至梅戍，蕃夷稍稍來謁，暉顧首領一人，指其佩劍曰：「此板橋王氏劍邪？

translations.literal: " He then raised more than a thousand troops. Reaching Mei garrison, tribesmen came to call one after another. Hui glanced at one chieftain, pointed at the sword at his belt, and said: "Is this a Banqiao Wang blade?
translations.idiomatic: " He raised a thousand-odd men. At Mei garrison tribesmen called in turn. Hui eyed one chief, pointed at his belt sword, and said: "A Banqiao Wang blade?

sentences.zh: 吾聞王氏劍天下利器也。

translations.literal: I have heard the Wang blade is the finest weapon under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Wang blades are the finest steel under heaven.

sentences.zh: 」俯而取諸腰間，若將玩之，因擊殺首領者，其從騎十餘人皆殺之。

translations.literal: " He bent and took it from the man’s waist as if to admire it, then struck and killed the chieftain, and killed more than ten of his mounted followers as well.
translations.idiomatic: " He bent as if to admire it, took it from the man’s belt, and killed the chief and a dozen of his riders besides.

sentences.zh: 裨將藥元福曰：「今去靈武尚五六百里，奈何？

translations.literal: Deputy Yao Yuanfu said: "We are still five or six hundred li from Lingwu—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Yao Yuanfu said: "Lingwu is still five or six hundred li off—what now?

sentences.zh: 」暉笑曰：「此夷落之豪，部族之所恃也，吾能殺之，其餘豈敢動哉！

translations.literal: " Hui laughed and said: "This is a chieftain of the tribes, the one the clans rely on. If I can kill him, how would the rest dare stir!
translations.idiomatic: " Hui laughed: "This was their great chief, the tribes’ pillar. Kill him and who dares move?

sentences.zh: 」已而諸族皆以兵扼道路，暉以言譬諭之，獨所殺首領一族求戰，即與之戰而敗走，諸族遂不敢動。

translations.literal: " Before long every tribe took up arms to block the road. Hui reasoned with them in words; only the clan of the slain chieftain sought battle. He fought them, they were beaten and fled, and the tribes then dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon every tribe barred the road. Hui talked them down; only the dead chief’s clan fought. He beat them off, and the rest held still.

sentences.zh: 暉至靈武，撫綏邊部，凡十餘年，恩信大著。

translations.literal: Hui reached Lingwu and soothed the border tribes for more than ten years; his kindness and trust became greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu he soothed the border tribes more than ten years until grace and trust shone wide.

sentences.zh: 官至中書令，封陳留王。

translations.literal: He rose to Grand Councilor and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Councilor and was enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年卒，追封衛王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun he died; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Guangshun and was posthumously made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 子繼業。

translations.literal: He had a son Jiye.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son Jiye.

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉

translations.literal: Huang Fuhui
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fuhui

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Huang Fuhui was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fuhui came from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 為魏軍卒，戍瓦橋關，歲滿當代歸，而留屯貝州。

translations.literal: He was a Wei soldier, garrisoned at Waqiao Pass; when his term ended he should have been relieved and sent home, but instead was left to garrison at Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was a Wei soldier at Waqiao Pass. His term ended and he should have gone home, but the army kept him at Bei.

sentences.zh: 是時，唐莊宗已失政，天下離心。

translations.literal: At that time Tang’s Zhuangzong had already lost good government, and the realm’s hearts were divided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had already lost the realm, and hearts everywhere pulled apart.

sentences.zh: 暉為人驍勇無賴，夜博軍中，不勝，乃與其徒謀為亂，劫其部將楊仁晟曰：「唐能破梁而得天下者，以先得魏而盡有河北兵也。

translations.literal: Fuhui was fierce and lawless. He gambled in camp at night, lost, and with his fellows plotted mutiny. They seized their commander Yang Rencheng and said: "Tang could break Liang and take the realm because it first took Wei and thereby held all the Hebei armies.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhui was brutal and reckless. He gambled in camp at night, lost, and with his mates plotted mutiny. They seized their officer Yang Rencheng and said: "Tang broke Liang because it took Wei first and held all Hebei arms.

sentences.zh: 魏軍甲不去體、馬不解鞍者十餘年，今天下已定，而天子不念魏軍久戍之勞，去家咫尺，不得相見。

translations.literal: Wei soldiers for more than ten years did not remove armor from their bodies or saddles from their horses. Now the realm is settled, yet the Son of Heaven does not remember the Wei army’s long garrison toil. Home is a foot away, yet they cannot see their kin.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years Wei men never stripped mail or ungirt saddles. The realm is settled, yet the throne forgets our long watch. Home is a step away and we cannot see kin.

sentences.zh: 今將士思歸不可遏，公當與我俱行。

translations.literal: The soldiers’ longing to return cannot be stopped. You must march with us.
translations.idiomatic: Our longing to return cannot be held. March with us.

sentences.zh: 不幸天子怒吾軍，則坐據一州，足以起事。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven should rage at our army, then sit and hold one prefecture—enough to raise an affair.
translations.idiomatic: If the throne rages at us, seize a prefecture and that is enough to rise.

sentences.zh: 」仁晟曰：「公等何計之過也！

translations.literal: " Rencheng said: "Your plans go too far! Now a brilliant lord sits above, the realm is one house, and keen armor and sharp weapons number no less than several hundred thousand. You each have families—why speak such ill-omened words?
translations.idiomatic: " Rencheng said: "You go too far! A bright lord rules, the realm is one house, and sharp arms number in the hundreds of thousands. You have kin—why such ill-omened talk?

sentences.zh: 今英主在上，天下一家，精甲銳兵，不下數十萬，公等各有家屬，何故出此不祥之言？

translations.literal: The soldiers knew they could not force him, so they beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The men knew he would not yield and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 」軍士知不可強，遂斬之，推一小校為主，不從，又斬之，乃攜二首以詣裨將趙在禮，在禮從之，乃夜焚貝州以入於魏，在禮以暉為馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: They pushed a junior officer to be leader; he would not obey, and they beheaded him too. Then carrying the two heads they went to deputy Zhao Zaili; Zaili followed them. That night they burned Bei prefecture and entered Wei; Zaili made Fuhui commander of the horse and foot army.
translations.idiomatic: They made a junior officer chief; he refused and they killed him too. With both heads they went to Zhao Zaili, who joined them. That night they burned Bei and entered Wei. Zaili made Fuhui horse-and-foot commander.

sentences.zh: 暉擁甲士數百騎，大掠城中，至一民家，問其姓，曰：「姓國。

translations.literal: Fuhui led several hundred armored horsemen and plundered greatly through the city. At one household he asked the surname; they said: "The surname is Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhui led hundreds of armored horse and plundered the city. At one house he asked the surname; they said: "Guo.

sentences.zh: 」暉曰：「吾當破國！

translations.literal: " Fuhui said: "I shall break the state!
translations.idiomatic: " Fuhui said: "I shall ruin the state!

sentences.zh: 」遂盡殺之。

translations.literal: " and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: " and killed them to the last.

sentences.zh: 又至一家，問其姓，曰：「姓萬。

translations.literal: At another household he asked the surname; they said: "The surname is Wan.
translations.idiomatic: At another house he asked; they said: "Wan.

sentences.zh: 」暉曰：「吾殺萬家足矣。

translations.literal: " Fuhui said: "Killing ten thousand households is enough for me.
translations.idiomatic: " Fuhui said: "Slaying ten thousand houses is enough.

sentences.zh: 」又盡殺之。

translations.literal: " and again killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: " and again killed them all.

sentences.zh: 及明宗入魏，遂與在禮合謀，莊宗之禍自暉始。

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered Wei, Fuhui joined Zaili in further plots, and Zhuangzong’s disaster began with Fuhui.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong entered Wei, Fuhui plotted on with Zaili, and Zhuangzong’s ruin began with Fuhui.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，暉自軍卒擢拜陳州刺史，終唐世常為刺史。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Fuhui was raised from a soldier to prefect of Chen and through the Tang age was often a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong raised him from the ranks to prefect of Chen, and through Tang he often held a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，以衛將軍居京師。

translations.literal: In Jin’s Tianfu era he was a guard general living in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Tianfu he was a guard general in the capital.

sentences.zh: 在禮已秉旄節，罷鎮來朝，暉往候之曰：「與公俱起甘陵，卒成大事，然由我發也，公今富貴，能恤我乎？

translations.literal: Zaili already held a military commission; when he left his post and came to court, Fuhui called on him and said: "You and I rose together at Ganling and at last achieved the great affair—but it began with me. You are rich and honored now; can you spare a thought for me?
translations.idiomatic: Zaili already held a commission and came to court on leave. Fuhui visited him: "We rose at Ganling and finished the great work, but I lit the fuse. You are rich now—will you spare me?

sentences.zh: 不然，禍起坐中！

translations.literal: If not, disaster will rise from this very seat!
translations.idiomatic: If not, ruin will rise from this seat!

sentences.zh: 」在禮懼，遽出器幣數千與之，而飲以酒，暉飲自若，不謝而去。

translations.literal: " Zaili was afraid and at once brought out several thousand in vessels and goods and gave them to him, then poured wine. Fuhui drank at ease and left without thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Zaili feared him, brought out thousands in goods at once, and poured wine. Fuhui drank easy and left without thanks.

sentences.zh: 久之，為密州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made prefect of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Long after he was made prefect of Mi.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯闕，暉率其州人奔於江南，李景以為歙州刺史、奉化軍節度使，鎮江州。

translations.literal: When the Khitan stormed the capital, Fuhui led his prefecture’s people south to the Yangtze. Li Jing made him prefect of She, military commissioner of the Fenghua army, and stationed him at Jiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took the capital, Fuhui fled south with his prefecture. Li Jing made him prefect of She and commissioner of Fenghua at Jiang.

sentences.zh: 周師征淮，景以暉為北面行營應援使，屯清流關，為周師所敗，並其都監姚鳳皆被擒。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops campaigned on the Huai, Jing made Fuhui northern relief commissioner of the field camp and stationed him at Qingliu Pass. Zhou troops defeated him and captured him together with his overseer Yao Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou marched on the Huai. Jing named Fuhui northern relief commissioner and posted him at Qingliu Pass. Zhou broke him and took him with his overseer Yao Feng.

sentences.zh: 世宗召見，暉金瘡被體，哀之，賜以金帶、鞍馬，後數日卒。

translations.literal: Shizong summoned him to audience. Fuhui’s body was covered with golden wounds; Shizong pitied him, bestowed a gold belt and saddle horse, and several days later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong called him in. Golden wounds covered him; Shizong pitied him, gave belt and horse, and he died days later.

sentences.zh: 拜鳳左屯衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Feng was made Senior General of the Left Stationed Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was made Senior General of the Left Stationed Guard.

sentences.zh: 唐景思

translations.literal: Tang Jingsi
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jingsi

sentences.zh: 唐景思，秦州人也。

translations.literal: Tang Jingsi was a native of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jingsi came from Qin.

sentences.zh: 幼善角觝，以屠狗為生。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at wrestling and made his living butchering dogs.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he wrestled well and butchered dogs for a living.

sentences.zh: 後去為軍卒，累遷指揮使。

translations.literal: Later he left home to become a soldier and was repeatedly promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became a soldier and rose to commander.

sentences.zh: 唐魏王繼岌伐蜀，景思為蜀守固鎮。

translations.literal: When Tang’s Prince of Wei Jiji attacked Shu, Jingsi was Shu defender of Guzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiji attacked Shu, Jingsi held Guzhen for Shu.

sentences.zh: 繼岌兵至，景思以城降，拜興州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jiji’s army arrived, Jingsi surrendered the city and was made prefect of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji arrived; Jingsi yielded the city and was made prefect of Xing.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，為貝州行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he was marching marshal of Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Gaozu he was Bei’s marching marshal.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，契丹攻陷貝州，景思為趙延壽所得，以為壕砦使。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor the Khitan attacked and took Bei prefecture; Jingsi was taken by Zhao Yanshou and made trench-works commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor the Khitan took Bei; Jingsi fell to Zhao Yanshou and was made trench commissioner.

sentences.zh: 契丹滅晉，拜景思亳州防禦使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Jingsi was made defender of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ended Jin, he was made defender of Bo.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖時，為鄧州行軍司馬，後為沿淮巡檢。

translations.literal: Under Han Gaozu he was marching marshal of Deng and later inspector along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Gaozu he was Deng’s marching marshal, then Huai river inspector.

sentences.zh: 漢法酷，而史弘肇用事，喜以告訐殺人。

translations.literal: Han law was harsh, and Shi Hongzhao held power, delighting in killing men on denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: Han law ran harsh. Shi Hongzhao held power and loved to kill on accusation.

sentences.zh: 景思有奴，嘗有所求不如意，即馳見弘肇，言景思與李景交通，而私畜兵甲。

translations.literal: Jingsi had a slave who, when a request went unmet, at once galloped to see Hongzhao and said Jingsi was in contact with Li Jing and privately stored arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsi had a slave whose wish went unmet; the man galloped to Hongzhao and said Jingsi trafficked with Li Jing and hid arms.

sentences.zh: 弘肇遣吏將三十騎往收景思，奴謂吏曰：「景思勇者也，得則殺之，不然將失之也。

translations.literal: Hongzhao sent officers with thirty horsemen to seize Jingsi. The slave told the officers: "Jingsi is a brave man—if you take him, kill him at once, or you will lose him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao sent thirty horse to seize him. The slave told them: "Jingsi is bold—take him and kill at once or you will lose him.

sentences.zh: 」吏至，景思迎前，以兩手抱吏呼冤，請詣獄自理。

translations.literal: " When the officers arrived, Jingsi came forward, embraced the officer with both arms, cried injustice, and asked to go to prison to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: " They came; Jingsi met them, seized the officer in both arms, cried injustice, and asked prison to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 吏引奴與景思驗，景思曰：「我家在此，請索之。

translations.literal: The officers brought the slave to confront Jingsi. Jingsi said: "My household is here—search it.
translations.idiomatic: They brought the slave to face him. Jingsi said: "My house is here—search it.

sentences.zh: 有錢十千，為受外賂。

translations.literal: There are ten thousand cash—proof I took outside bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand cash—that is outside bribe.

sentences.zh: 有甲一屬，為私畜兵。

translations.literal: There is one suit of armor—proof I privately stored troops.
translations.idiomatic: One suit of mail—that is private arms.

sentences.zh: 」吏索之，惟一衣笥，軍籍、糧簿而已。

translations.literal: " The officers searched and found only one clothes basket, military registers, and grain ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: " They searched and found only one clothes chest, muster rolls, and grain books.

sentences.zh: 吏閔而寬之，景思請械送京師以自明。

translations.literal: The officers pitied him and relented. Jingsi asked to be sent in fetters to the capital to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: The officers pitied him and eased off. Jingsi asked fetters and the capital to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 景思有仆王知權在京師，聞景思被告，乃見弘肇，願先下獄明景思不反，弘肇憐之，送知權獄中，日勞以酒食。

translations.literal: Jingsi had a servant Wang Zhiquan in the capital who, hearing Jingsi was accused, went to see Hongzhao and wished to enter prison first to prove Jingsi did not rebel. Hongzhao pitied him and sent Zhiquan into prison, daily treating him with wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Servant Wang Zhiquan was in the capital; hearing the charge, he saw Hongzhao and offered prison first to prove no revolt. Hongzhao pitied him and jailed Zhiquan, daily feeding him wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 景思既械就道，潁、亳之人隨至京師共明之。

translations.literal: Once Jingsi was fettered on the road, people of Ying and Bo followed him to the capital together to clear him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsi went fettered; men of Ying and Bo followed to the capital to clear him.

sentences.zh: 弘肇乃鞫其奴，具伏，即奏斬奴而釋景思。

translations.literal: Hongzhao then interrogated the slave; he confessed fully. Hongzhao at once memorialized to behead the slave and release Jingsi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao examined the slave; he confessed all. Hongzhao memorialized, beheaded the slave, and freed Jingsi.

sentences.zh: 後從世宗戰高平，世宗以所得漢降兵數千為效順指揮，以景思為指揮使，復戍淮上。

translations.literal: Later he followed Shizong at the battle of Gaoping. Shizong made several thousand Han surrender troops into the Obedient Command and made Jingsi its commander, again garrisoning him on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Shizong at Gaoping. Shizong formed several thousand Han surrender troops into the Obedient Command, made Jingsi commander, and posted him again on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 周師伐淮南，以功領饒州刺史，遷濠州刺史，兵攻濠州，以戰傷重卒，贈武清軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhou armies campaigned against Huainan, for merit he was made prefect of Rao, then transferred to Hao prefecture; troops attacked Hao prefecture, and he died of severe battle wounds; he was posthumously made military commissioner of Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou armies marched on Huainan, merit made him Rao prefect, then Hao prefect. Enemy troops struck Hao; he died of his wounds and was posthumously made military commissioner of Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 予述舊史，至於王進之事，未嘗不廢書而嘆曰：甚哉，五代之君，皆武人崛起，其所與俱勇夫悍卒，各裂土地封侯王，何異豺狼之牧斯人也！

translations.literal: When I set down the old histories and came to Wang Jin’s story, I never failed to lay aside the book and sigh: How extreme! The rulers of the Five Dynasties all rose as men of war; the fierce soldiers and brutal troops who rose with them each carved out land and were enfeoffed as marquises and kings—how unlike wolves herding men!
translations.idiomatic: When I set down the old histories and came to Wang Jin, I never failed to lay aside the book and sigh: How extreme! Every ruler of the Five Dynasties was a warrior risen from the ranks; the bold and brutal men who rose with him carved out domains and were made marquises and kings—what but wolves herding sheep?

sentences.zh: 雖其附托遭遇，出於一時之幸，然猶必皆橫身陣敵，非有百夫之勇，則必一日之勞。

translations.literal: Though their patronage and fortune came from a moment’s luck, they still had to throw themselves into battle—without the courage of a hundred men, at least a day’s labor in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Even when favor and fortune came from a moment’s luck, they still had to throw themselves into the line—without the strength of a hundred men, at least a day’s worth of fighting.

sentences.zh: 至如進者，徒以疾足善走而秉旄節，何其甚歟！

translations.literal: As for Jin, he held a commissioner’s baton merely for swift feet and a gift for running—how extreme is that!
translations.idiomatic: Jin held a commissioner’s baton for nothing but swift feet and a gift for running—how extreme is that!

sentences.zh: 豈非名器之用，隨世而輕重者歟？

translations.literal: Is it not that the weight of rank and title shifts with the age?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that rank and title grow light or heavy with the times?

sentences.zh: 世治則君子居之而重，世亂則小人易得而輕歟？

translations.literal: When the age is well ordered, gentlemen hold them and they weigh heavy; when the age is chaotic, petty men obtain them easily and they weigh light?
translations.idiomatic: In ordered times gentlemen hold them and they weigh heavy; in chaotic times petty men seize them easily and they weigh light?

sentences.zh: 抑因緣僥幸，未始不有，而尤多於亂世，既其極也，遂至於是歟？

translations.literal: Or is it that chance and luck have never been absent, but abound above all in chaotic ages—and at the extreme, things come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it that luck has never been absent, but runs riot in chaotic ages—and at the extreme, things come to this?

sentences.zh: 豈其又有甚於是者歟？

translations.literal: And are there yet cases worse than this?
translations.idiomatic: And are there yet cases worse than this?

sentences.zh: 當此之時，為國長者不過十餘年，短者三四年至一二年。

translations.literal: In that age, a man who held the state did so for no more than a dozen years—at shortest three or four years, or one or two.
translations.idiomatic: In that age the longest reign was barely a dozen years; the shortest ran three or four, or one or two.

sentences.zh: 天下之人，視其上易君代國，如更戍長無異，蓋其輕如此，況其下者乎！

translations.literal: Men under heaven watched their superiors change rulers and dynasties as casually as a garrison chief is replaced—so lightly were they held; how much more those below!
translations.idiomatic: Men under heaven watched their betters change rulers and dynasties as casually as a garrison chief is rotated—so lightly were they held; how much more those below!

sentences.zh: 如進等者，豈足道哉！

translations.literal: Men like Jin—what is there to speak of!
translations.idiomatic: Men like Jin—what is there to speak of!

sentences.zh: 《易》否泰消長，君子小人常相上下，視在上者如進等，則其在下者可知矣。

translations.literal: In the Changes, pi and tai wax and wane; gentleman and petty man constantly trade places above and below. When those on high are like Jin, those below may be known.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes tells how pi and tai wax and wane and gentleman and petty man trade places. When those on high are like Jin, those below may be guessed.

sentences.zh: 予書進事，所以哀斯人之亂，而見當時賢人君子之在下者，可勝道哉！

translations.literal: I record Jin’s story to mourn the chaos of that age—and to show how many worthy gentlemen and scholars of the time were kept below. What sighs could number them all!
translations.idiomatic: I record Jin’s story to mourn that chaos—and to show how many worthy men were kept below. What sighs could number them all!

sentences.zh: 可勝道哉！

translations.literal: What sighs could number them all!
translations.idiomatic: What sighs could number them all!

sentences.zh: 孫方諫

translations.literal: Sun Fangjian
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fangjian

sentences.zh: 孫方諫，鄭州清苑人也。

translations.literal: Sun Fangjian was a man of Qingyuan in Zheng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fangjian came from Qingyuan in Zheng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，定州西北有狼山堡，定人常保以避契丹，有尼深意居其中，以佛法誘民，民多歸之。

translations.literal: At first, northwest of Ding prefecture there was Langshan Fort; the people of Ding often sheltered there to escape the Khitan. A nun named Shenyi lived within it and drew the people by Buddhist teaching; many followed her.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Ding stood Langshan Fort, where Ding people sheltered from the Khitan. A nun, Shenyi, lived there and drew folk by Buddhist teaching; many followed her.

sentences.zh: 後尼死，堡人言其屍不朽，因奉而事之。

translations.literal: When the nun died, the fort people said her corpse did not decay, and they honored and served her.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, the fort folk said her body did not decay and they honored and served her.

sentences.zh: 尼姓孫氏，方諫自以為尼族人，即繼行其法，堡人推以為主。

translations.literal: The nun’s surname was Sun; Fangjian took himself for kin of the nun’s clan, then carried on her practices, and the fort people pushed him as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: The nun was surnamed Sun; Fangjian claimed her clan, carried on her practices, and the fort folk made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 晉出帝時，義武軍節度使惡方諫聚徒山中，恐為邊患，因表以為遊奕使。

translations.literal: In the Last Emperor’s time of Jin, the military commissioner of the Yiwu army hated Fangjian for gathering followers in the hills and feared a border trouble; he therefore memorialized to make him roving patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Last Emperor the Yiwu commissioner hated Fangjian for gathering men in the hills and feared border trouble; he memorialized to make him roving patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 方諫因有所求不得，乃北通契丹。

translations.literal: Fangjian, because a request went unanswered, then opened relations with the Khitan in the north.
translations.idiomatic: When a request went unanswered, Fangjian turned to the Khitan in the north.

sentences.zh: 契丹後滅晉，以方諫為義武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Afterward the Khitan destroyed Jin and made Fangjian military commissioner of the Yiwu army.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan later destroyed Jin and made Fangjian military commissioner of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 已而徙方諫於雲中，方諫不受命，率其徒復入狼山。

translations.literal: Soon they moved Fangjian to Yunzhong; Fangjian would not accept the order and led his followers back into Langshan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they moved him to Yunzhong; he refused and led his band back into Langshan Fort.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖起，契丹縱火燒定州，虜其人民北去。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu rose; the Khitan set fire to Ding prefecture and carried its people north as captives.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu rose; the Khitan burned Ding prefecture and drove its people north as captives.

sentences.zh: 方諫聞之，自狼山入，據之以歸漢，高祖嘉之，即拜方諫義武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Fangjian heard of it, he came out from Langshan, seized the place, and submitted to Han; Gaozu praised him and at once made him military commissioner of the Yiwu army.
translations.idiomatic: Fangjian marched out of Langshan, seized the city, and submitted to Han; Gaozu praised him and at once restored him as Yiwu commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周太祖時，徙鎮鎮國，以其弟行友為定州留後。

translations.literal: Under Zhou Taizu he was moved to Zhenguo, and his younger brother Xingyou was made acting governor of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Taizu he was moved to Zhenguo; his younger brother Xingyou was left as acting governor of Ding.

sentences.zh: 世宗攻太原，方諫朝於行在，從還京，至洛得疾，徙鎮匡國，卒於洛陽，年六十二，贈太師。

translations.literal: When Shizong attacked Taiyuan, Fangjian came to court at the imperial camp, followed him back to the capital, fell ill at Luoyang, was moved to Kuangguo, and died at Luoyang at the age of sixty-two; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong attacked Taiyuan, Fangjian came to the imperial camp, followed him home, fell ill at Luoyang, was moved to Kuangguo, and died there at sixty-two; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
